candidates.title: The keyboard shortcuts panel toggle button is not displayed in Chrome
candidates.reason: Chrome touch-device condition; no named stable working pair or applicable fix established; frozen PRESS does not include question mark.
candidates.issueBody:
**react-dates version**
e.g. react-dates@20.1.0

**Describe the bug**
The keyboard shortcuts panel toggle button (right bottom corner triangle with question mark) is not displayed in Chrome. It is displayed in Firefox. It's completely missing in the DOM in Chrome and pressing the question mark also doesn't open the info panel.

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Windows 10
 - Browser: Chrome 75.0.3770.100

**Is the issue reproducible in Storybook?**
Yes. In every story.

**Additional context**
I have hybrid notebook with touch screen and external display. If you try to detect something as if the device is touch or not this might be an important information. (And your solution not working correctly in that case.)
I suggest making the button appear only when focused and hide it visually in other cases. You should rather use approach similar to `sr-only-focusable` in Bootstrap 4. Hiding the button via any JS condition is not necessary and won't cover all the cases. It can be in the DOM all the time, like the skip links etc. This is a common and correct approach.

candidates.title: showYearDropdown and showMonthYearDropdown are not accessible via keyboard
candidates.reason: Longstanding dropdown a11y issue; no working stable baseline established.
candidates.issueBody:
**Describe the bug**
Year (`showYearDropdown`=true) and month-year (`showMonthYearDropdown`=true) dropdowns are not accessible via keyboard

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
- Go to https://codesandbox.io/s/zen-tesla-86xt77?file=/src/App.js:514-535
- Tab into either datepicker input field.
- When the calendar popup appears, start tabbing through the elements.

You will not be able to tab into the year or month dropdowns

**Expected behavior**
You can tab to the year/month-year dropdown as well as the calendar days, previous month, next month.

**Additional context**
This was found during an a11y audit, here's the text of their finding:
> Issue: The dropdowns for selecting Month/Year within the datepicker are not keyboard accessible. When focused on the screen reader using the arrow keys, they are announced without a role.
> Why it matters: Proper implementation of a combobox ensures that screen reader users and those relying on keyboard navigation can perceive and operate its functionality effectively. This enables all users to select options smoothly. 
> How to fix it: Consider implementing the control as a single-selection combobox. Use the WAI-ARIA examples and patterns as a reference for proper implementation.

This is a rereport of https://github.com/Hacker0x01/react-datepicker/issues/4127

candidates.title: Arrow-navigation in calendar does not change focus, breaking accessibility
candidates.reason: Unsplit fixture under batch24: source-supported6.9.0/7.0.0/fixed8.2.0 hypothesis; checks pending.
candidates.issueBody:
**Describe the bug**
When you open the calendar and use the arrow keys to navigate to a new day, the focused element does not change.

This has 2 important consequences that I'm aware of:
1. Screen-reader accessibility for the calendar is broken. When screen-reader user uses arrow-key to navigate to a new day, there will be 0 announcements.

2. `:focus` and `:focus-visible` pseudo-selectors will not apply to a day that has been selected via arrow keys.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. run the following script:
`function printFocusedElement() {
  console.log(document.activeElement);
  setTimeout(printFocusedElement, 2000); 
}
printFocusedElement();` 


2. Use an arrow-key to navigate to a new day in react-datepicker calendar
3. Note that the focused element being logged has not changed

**Expected behavior**
When you use arrow-key to navigate to a day, that day should be focused.

**Screenshots**
In this screenshot, I have navigated from February 19th --> February 17th via arrow-keys, but February 19th is still the focused element.
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cb0119e3-b3e5-43e4-b477-c2893a437415)



**Desktop (please complete the following information):**
- OS: [Windows]
- Browser [Chrome]
- Version [132.0.6834.197]

**Additional context**

This behavior first appears in react-datepicker v7.0.0 


This only applies when using arrow keys to navigate between days in the same month. The focus is still applied correctly when you navigate from a day in month X to a day in Month Y using arrow-keys. 

Additionally, if you tab from the `next-month` button to the day, it will be focused correctly. 
(ex: 
navigate to a from May 20 to May 19 via arrows.  May 19 will not be focused.
hit TAB. You are now on the 'previous-month' button. 
hit TAB again. You are now on 'next-month' button. 
hit TAB again. You are now on May 19, and now it it focused. 
)

comments.body: @martijnrusschen It looks like a regression occurred, causing the calendar in the last two major versions to be essentially completely inaccessible.

@mellis481 @John-Feola 
Perhaps adding `containerRef={this.containerRef}` to the following link and adjusting the type will make it work correctly.
However, I am not sure because it has been a while since I ran it, and I am unable to debug it properly in my local environment.

https://github.com/Hacker0x01/react-datepicker/blob/cd1789c1de51a4a850da07ea32dbbc5b2f115c45/src/calendar.tsx#L994

> However, I am not sure because it has been a while since I ran it, and I am unable to debug it properly in my local environment.

@yuki0410-dev Can you clarify why you're saying you can't investigate the issue? To be clear, the issue in your PR has effectively made the calendar completely inaccessible. It would be great to get your involvement in this since you are most familiar with your own code.

@mellis481 

I have built a new environment according to CONTRIBUTING.md and tried debugging with console.log in my local docs-site, but the console.log results do not show up in the browser console.
Any advice on this? (When I was a previous contributor, RCA was installed, not vite, and it worked fine.)

Just to let you know, I am only one of about 400 contributors to this repository, so I can't always keep up with the latest developments in this repository.

The above response was not sufficient.
The following PR may have involved the splitting of the Calendar.tsx div ref into a separate component.
Unlike state, containerRef does not trigger re-rendering, so there are cases where child component props are not updated even if they are updated on a delay.

https://github.com/Hacker0x01/react-datepicker/pull/4979
@yuki0410-dev I want to make sure I'm interpreting your comment correct. Are you asserting that the issue is caused by #4979 and not #4766?

@mellis481 

First, containerRef is no longer passed from Calendar to Month in #4766.
At this point, we believe we could have fixed the problem by just fixing the passing of containerRef from Calendar to Month.
(I believe this was both an inadvertent error on my part and the reviewer's, and also a test case coverage issue.)

Secondly, I believe that the problem in this issue is complicated by the fact that in #4979, the containerRef is set from a div in the calendar component to a ClickOutsideWrapper, which changes the timing of when current is updated. The issue is complicated by the fact that the current is updated at different times.

We have implemented a fix to the first issue and created a PR for #5456.
(We have not yet been able to confirm the test).
However, we have not been able to resolve the issue in this issue, and further testing is required.

In addition to #5456, one of the following fixes would resolve the events in this issue, but we feel that none of them are a good approach.

 Method 1
Place a div inside the ClickOutsideWrapper of the Calendar component.
Keep the ref of that div in the Calendar component and pass it to the Month component instead of the containerRef.

Method 2
Make the key of the part of the Week component that calls the Day component always be changed.
Example: `key={day.valueOf() + new Date().valueOf()}`.

Any good advice would be appreciated.
Thanks! @yuki0410-dev

candidates.reason: Mobile virtual keyboard outside frozen context.
candidates.issueBody:
![keyboard-on-focus](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1021849/33655739-39528700-da74-11e7-86c0-8190ca20ad70.png)

Strange... I see this problem was previously reported on #100, but I do get this problem with `"react-day-picker": "^7.0.5"` (upgraded from `6.2.1` 30 mins ago).

Isn't anyone else getting this problem? The implementation is done through a **DayPickerInput** component.

comments.body: @dreamyguy the input component always worked like this on mobile. Could you show us the code that was working with v6? Maybe you were passing props to the input component that now should be passed via `inputProps`?

Sorry I could have been clearer. It was not working on v6 either, so I upgraded to see if it was working with v7. So no changes there.

I got the impression on #100 that this was not an issue with DayPickerInput, as another user suggested the screenshot taken was from another component/project.

So I guess there's no way around it, then?
Duplicate of https://github.com/gpbl/react-day-picker/issues/583

For reference, I'd just like to point out that passing the property `readOnly: true` through `inputProps` made the input get the `readonly` attribute that prevents direct user input on the input field.

This is great because the keyboard will no longer be triggered on mobile, and therefore will not cover the calendar. This also improve input validation for those who must have it. ✨ 

```
<DayPickerInput
  inputProps={{ readOnly: true }}
  placeholder="DD/MM/YYYY"
  format="DD/MM/YYYY"
/>
```

Change the input style (like `cursor: pointer`) and you'll end up with an input that will be experienced more like a button.

Big thanks to @gpbl who guided me in the right direction.
Thanks for writing back @dreamyguy !

candidates.title: Simulating focusing and pressing Enter on a disabled date causes it to appear enabled and fires onSelect in 9.11.2 but didn't in 9.11.1
candidates.reason: Maintainer states only JSDOM tests affected, not end users.
candidates.issueBody:
## To reproduce

* Render a react-day-picker with disabled dates, like `disabled={[{before: some-date}]}` in a testing-library test
* Call `act(() => disabledElement.focus());` on a disabled element
* Call `expect(disabledElement).toBeDisabled();` fails. 
* Also simulating a user pressing enter (`await user.keyboard("{enter}")`) will fire the `onSelect` function

This didn't used to happen in 9.11.1. But does in 9.11.2. I assume this is as a result of the change in [this commit](https://github.com/gpbl/react-day-picker/commit/1dececbb93a99571f61ebcd6f0b89323c24e7a21).

The clear ✖️ button is interact-able via the keyboard.

### Actual Result
The clear ✖️ button is not interact-able via the keyboard.

0.85.0

https://codesandbox.io/s/7mr7p7zwy6

candidates.title: Unpredictable 'valueBeforeUpDown' when using keyboard + mouse together
candidates.reason: Original primary task mixes pointer mouseover with keys; pure keyboard reproduction and working boundary absent.
candidates.issueBody:
Not sure if this is a bug or intended behavior, but it seems odd to me. You can see it in your codepen here: http://codepen.io/moroshko/pen/PZWbzK
1. Focus on the input field
2. Type `c`, and wait for suggestions to appear
3. <kbd>ArrowDown</kbd> to any option
4. Mouseover/move over the suggestion list 
   
   **Observed behaviour:** You should notice the one you have highlighted has the whole word highlighted now, and the input value change as well (but the suggestions don't update to reflect this).
   
   **Expected behaviour:** Not quite sure, but I feel like it should behave the same as key up/down and not update the input value. Maybe valueBeforeUpDown should not be updated if it's via mouseevent.

Let me know if you think this is a bug or not, or maybe an unimportant edge case. I am doing some extra stuff on mouseenter/leave of each suggestion, so it's quite noticeable for me.

Caused by a combo of:

`
onMouseLeave: this.resetFocusedSuggestion,
`
...
`
resetFocusedSuggestion = () => {
    this.props.updateFocusedSuggestion(null, null);
  };
`

Since it's null now, it grabs the input value instead of the correct previous value.
`
    const renderSuggestionData = {
      query: (valueBeforeUpDown || value).trim()
    };
`

If [onSuggestionFocused](https://github.com/moroshko/react-autosuggest/issues/168) is implemented, this could be squashed at the same time.

comments.body: This is fixed in [v7.0.1](https://github.com/moroshko/react-autosuggest/releases/tag/v7.0.1) now.
Thanks @moroshko! Will test it out this week and let you know if there are any other issues related to this.

candidates.title: Component requires double Tab press to advance focus (with no interactions)
candidates.reason: Reporter confirms custom suggestion component caused behavior.
candidates.issueBody:
### Background

I have been trying to use the AutoSuggest component to create a wrapper to add some predefined and "extended" functionality for our app. I have been really appreciating the accessibility of the component (enabling keyboard/mouse interactions fluently) but have discovered a possible issue with tab-to-advance (in specific conditions).

If a user is tabbing through a form, when the focus reaches the AutoComplete it will automatically open the suggestion list (good). However, assuming the user **does not interact** with the component, the next <kbd>Tab</kbd> press will simply close the suggestions list and **not advance** to the next component. Pressing <kbd>Tab</kbd> again will advance to the next component as normal. Strangely, reversing through the order works perfectly with <kbd>Shift + Tab</kbd> and the component will open the suggestions list upon receiving focus and close it **and** move to the previous component if the keys are pressed again.

**Additional Details:**

- Suggestion list renders upon focus
- When search text is the same as previously selected value, all suggestions are displayed (only matching ones otherwise)
- Custom input is wrapped in an HOC to manage the UI (border when focused). The HOC has hooks for `onBlur` and `onFocus` (changes the border colour, helps with "testing" focus)

### CodePen

- I was unable to replicate this issue in a CodePen at the moment which makes me wonder if it is something in our wrapper component. However, we are using a possibly unique combination (but not likely) of parameters which may introduce an edge case.

### Steps to Reproduce:

- Component has `shouldRenderSuggestions={true}`

1. Focus on the input field (_selections display_)
2. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> without interacting otherwise (_menu closes but focus doesn't appear to shift_)
3. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> again (_focus now shifts to next element, menu opens_)
4. Press <kbd>Shift + Tab</kbd> (_focus shifts back immediately, current menu closes and new menu opens_)

**Observed behaviour:** If no interaction is provided, focus doesn't immediately shift to next focusable element after the selections close (_with suggestions displaying on focus_).

**Expected behaviour:** Focus should immediately shift to the next focusable element after the selections close.

comments.body: As it turns out there was a custom component that we were rendering for the Suggestion item that caused this issue. Replacing it with a `div` solved the problem.
